title: Scenes on the Mac scene host bring their async-profiler output back: the profile run-scene reports exists after shutdown, at the local path it named
user-messages: profile on this machine if necessary, dont just blindly go chaning things
[recalled] after you are done make a ticket about this (said of: the scene host doesn't save the profile)
description:
Found on VIEW-31 (2026-11-07) while chasing a ~0.45 s stall when the ring scene switches between a dark and a paper look on IMG_4111.

On a worktree whose tmp/scene-host.json names the Mac (TOOL-52), `ixdar-cli run-scene` starts the JVM with `-agentpath:<mac>/ixd-scenes/<wt>/.profiler/libasyncProfiler=start,event=cpu,file=<mac>/ixd-scenes/<wt>/tmp/profiles/ring-tool-<stamp>-%p.html` and its reply names `"profile": ".../tmp/profiles/ring-tool-<stamp>-<pid>.html"`. After `ixdar-cli shutdown` no such file exists on Linux, and the Mac has no `ixd-scenes/<wt>/tmp/profiles` directory at all. `--profile-path tmp/view-31-palette.collapsed` behaved the same: the reply echoed the path, nothing was written on either machine. Locally run scenes (F5, `ixd wt done`'s launch) do leave tmp/profiles/f5-*.html, so the gap is the scene-host path.

Likely causes, not verified: the supervisor (`.ixd-scene-supervisor.sh`) or the shutdown route ends the JVM in a way that skips async-profiler's write at exit, and/or nothing copies tmp/profiles back the way screenshots and logs are. The Mac has only the agent library (`.profiler/libasyncProfiler`), no `asprof`, so a live scene cannot be dumped by hand either.

Workaround used: `jcmd <pid> JFR.start settings=profile filename=/tmp/x.jfr`, drive the scene, `jcmd <pid> JFR.stop`, then the JDK's `jfr print --events jdk.ExecutionSample` on the Mac and a small aggregation on Linux. That found the stall (94% of render-thread samples in MeshLabels.resolve -> RingRegions.nearestActiveFace), but it needs the java pid (pgrep on the supervisor's shell picks the wrong process) and a hand-written parser. Profiling a scene on the scene host should be as easy as profiling a local one, since the scans that need profiling are the ones too large to run locally.
definition-of-done:
1. `ixdar-cli run-scene` on a scene-host worktree, then `ixdar-cli shutdown`: the profile the reply named exists at that local path (default tmp/profiles/<scene>-<stamp>-<pid>.html), non-empty, with frames from the run.
2. `--profile-path <file>` and `--profile-event alloc` are honoured on the scene host as they are locally (the extension still picks the format, e.g. .collapsed).
3. A scene that dies or is killed still leaves whatever the profiler had, or the reply says plainly that no profile was written and why.
4. A test of the copy-back and path mapping that needs no Mac (the remote side faked as TOOL-52's tests do).
testing-plan:
1. The copy-back and path-mapping test.
2. On the Mac: run-scene IMG_4111 in the ring scene, switch looks a few times, shutdown; open the profile and find the render thread's frames.
3. The same with --profile-path tmp/x.collapsed and --profile-event alloc.
